# ExyokiOffice full AI context

> ExyokiOffice is a C++20 shared library for creating, opening, editing, and
> saving `.docx`, `.xlsx`, and `.pptx` Office Open XML packages. It directly
> reads and writes ZIP/XML packages and does not require Microsoft Office or
> .NET. This file is a self-contained orientation for AI systems; consult the
> linked source documentation for detailed feature contracts.

## Fast decision guide

Use the highest-level API that represents the task:

| Goal | Primary entry point | Main guide | Runnable example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Create or edit Word | `ExyokiOffice::Word::WordDocumentEditor` | `docs/Word.md`, `docs/word/` | `examples/ExampleWordEditor/main.cpp` |
| Modify an existing Word file | `WordDocumentEditor::Open`, `BodyCursor` | `docs/word/documents.md`, `docs/word/text.md` | `examples/ExampleWordEdit/main.cpp` |
| Create or edit Excel | `ExyokiOffice::Excel::ExcelDocumentEditor` | `docs/Excel.md`, `docs/excel/` | `examples/ExampleExcelEditor/main.cpp` |
| Create or edit PowerPoint | `ExyokiOffice::PowerPoint::PowerPointDocumentEditor` | `docs/PowerPoint.md`, `docs/powerpoint/` | `examples/ExamplePowerPointEditor/main.cpp` |
| Work with exact OpenXML elements | `OpenXmlElement` and generated DOM types | `docs/introduction.md` | `examples/ExampleWord/main.cpp` |
| Manipulate parts and relationships | `OpenXmlPackage`, `OpenXmlPackagePart`, `Packaging::*Document` | `docs/introduction.md` | `examples/ExampleWord/main.cpp` |
| Inspect, validate, convert, diff, or query | `ExyokiOffice::Tools`, `ExyokiOffice::Xml`, `exyoki` | `docs/tools/exyoki.md` | `tools/exyoki/main.cpp` |
| Signatures and external resources | `ExyokiOffice::Security` | `docs/Signatures.md`, `docs/ExternalResources.md` | focused unit tests |
| Change generated DOM behavior | generator under `gen/` | `gen/README.md`, `data/README.md` | generator unit tests |

Do not start with the generated DOM merely because Office Open XML is an XML
format. The hand-written editors preserve package invariants and provide safer,
shorter operations for modeled features.

## Product scope

ExyokiOffice supports three related but distinct layers:

1. Hand-written high-level editing APIs for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
2. Strongly typed OpenXML element classes generated from schema metadata.
3. Open Packaging Conventions infrastructure for ZIP parts, relationships,
   content types, and document lifecycle.

The `exyoki` executable is a thin command-line adapter over reusable library
modules. It can inspect packages, list parts and relationships, read properties,
validate (several files at once, expanding `*`/`?` wildcards itself), unpack
and repack, convert to and from Flat OPC, convert documents to semantic
Markdown/JSON/XML/text (plus CSV for workbooks), export media, search and
replace text across Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, redact comments, tracked
revisions, hidden text and identity metadata, fill Word mail-merge templates
from JSON, recalculate workbook formulas, compare Word documents into tracked
revisions, query XPath, extract text, split, merge, diff, inspect external
resources and signatures, and print shell completion scripts.
`exyoki commands --format json` describes the whole interface — commands,
options, value constraints and exit codes — so it can be discovered without
parsing `--help`. `exyoki schema` does the same for the data: it prints the
draft-07 JSON Schema of the semantic `convert` envelope (published as
`docs/schemas/exyokioffice-document-v1.schema.json`), and
`exyoki schema --check <file>` validates a generated document against it,
exiting `3` with one diagnostic per violation, each carrying the JSON pointer
of the offending value.

The library does not render documents, paginate text, calculate Word layout,
run VBA, automate Microsoft Office, or convert to PDF/HTML through a rendering
engine. Semantic conversions are deliberately lossy and report unsupported
content. Consult `docs/Compatibility.md` for precise feature depth and Office
version support.

## Main public classes

### Word

`ExyokiOffice::Word::WordDocumentEditor`, declared in
`include/ExyokiOffice/Word/WordDocument.hpp`, is the normal Word entry point.
It covers document lifecycle, paragraphs, runs, formatting, styles, headings,
lists, tables, images, hyperlinks, bookmarks, fields, sections, headers and
footers, notes, comments, content controls, revisions, protection, charts, and
document insertion or merging.

Body insertion uses cursors such as `Body()`, `Before(...)`, and `After(...)`.
Use these instead of manually finding and inserting WordprocessingML nodes when
the high-level operation exists.

```cpp
#include "ExyokiOffice/Word/WordDocument.hpp"

using namespace ExyokiOffice::Word;

auto editor = WordDocumentEditor::CreateNew();
if (!editor)
{
    return 1;
}

editor->AddHeading("Quarterly report");
editor->AddParagraph("Created by ExyokiOffice.");
if (!editor->SaveToFile("report.docx"))
{
    return 1;
}
```

Use `WordDocumentEditor::Open(...)` to modify an existing file. The
`examples/ExampleWordEdit/main.cpp` example demonstrates placeholders spanning
multiple runs, insertion next to existing blocks, and extending a table.

The lower-level `ExyokiOffice::Packaging::WordDocument` handles package
lifecycle and Word parts. It is re-exported as `ExyokiOffice::Word::WordDocument`.

### Excel

`ExyokiOffice::Excel::ExcelDocumentEditor`, declared in
`include/ExyokiOffice/Excel/ExcelDocument.hpp`, is the normal workbook entry
point. It covers worksheets, cells and ranges, shared strings, formulas and
recalculation, named ranges, styles and number formats, tables, auto-filters,
charts, pivot tables, slicers, validation, conditional formatting, structural
row and column edits, comments, images, and print layout.

```cpp
#include "ExyokiOffice/Excel/ExcelDocument.hpp"

using namespace ExyokiOffice::Excel;

auto editor = ExcelDocumentEditor::CreateNew();
if (!editor)
{
    return 1;
}

auto sheet = editor->FirstWorksheet();
sheet->SetCellText(1, 1, "Item");
sheet->SetCellText(1, 2, "Amount");
sheet->SetCellText(2, 1, "Example");
sheet->SetCellNumber(2, 2, 42.0);
if (!editor->SaveToFile("report.xlsx"))
{
    return 1;
}
```

The lower-level `ExyokiOffice::Packaging::ExcelDocument` handles workbook
package lifecycle and is re-exported in the Excel namespace.

### PowerPoint

`ExyokiOffice::PowerPoint::PowerPointDocumentEditor`, declared in
`include/ExyokiOffice/PowerPoint/PowerPointDocument.hpp`, is the normal
presentation entry point. It covers slides, masters, layouts, placeholders,
shape trees, geometry, transforms, fills, outlines, effects, text, pictures,
media, DrawingML tables, charts, transitions, animations, speaker notes,
comments, sections, and custom shows.

PowerPoint has an explicit master-layout-slide hierarchy. A new presentation
must provide a layout and master before associating a slide with that layout.
`CreateSlideBuilder()` offers a higher-level path for common title, text, and
shape construction.

The lower-level `ExyokiOffice::Packaging::PowerPointDocument` handles
presentation package lifecycle and is re-exported in the PowerPoint namespace.

## Cross-cutting API conventions

- Packages are loaded completely into memory. Editing mutates the in-memory
  model. Nothing reaches disk until `SaveToFile` or `SaveToMemory`.
- File saving is atomic by default: the old file is replaced only after the new
  package has been written successfully.
- Factories including `CreateNew`, `Open`, and many `Add...` methods return a
  null smart pointer when input cannot be read or an operation is invalid.
- More complex fallible operations return structured result types with an
  error code and message. Check `Succeeded()` or boolean conversion.
- Validating mutations should reject bad input before changing the document.
- Lengths use `MeasuringUnits` and explicit units. Angles use
  `MeasuringAngle`. General colors use `ExyokiOffice::Color`; formats may add
  their own color wrappers.
- Public declarations use integer, floating-point, size, and byte aliases from
  `ExyokiOffice/StandardTypes.hpp`.
- Preserve content that the high-level API does not interpret. An edit to one
  modeled feature must not silently discard unrelated parts or markup.
- `OpenSettings` controls validation and package safety limits for untrusted
  inputs. Do not assume unlimited package sizes are appropriate for a service.
- External resources are never fetched automatically. An application must
  explicitly install both a resolver and an allow policy.

One package and its complete object graph form one synchronization domain.
Editors, packages, parts, DOM elements, worksheets, slides, cursors, wrappers,
and borrowed views from that graph are not thread-safe. Confine the graph to
one thread or serialize every access with one application-owned mutex. Distinct
packages may be processed concurrently, provided they do not race on shared
application state or the same output path. See `docs/Threading.md` for the full
contract, cancellation pattern, and callback requirements.

## Typed DOM and packaging

The typed DOM namespace begins at
`ExyokiOffice::DocumentFormat::OpenXml`. Generated classes model elements,
attributes, enums, and content models for WordprocessingML, SpreadsheetML, and
PresentationML. `OpenXmlElement` supplies common tree operations. Use targeted
symbol searches rather than reading the full generated tree.

The packaging layer models an Office file as an OPC ZIP package containing
parts. Relationships connect packages or parts to other parts and to external
targets; content types tell consumers how each part is interpreted. A new
feature may require all of the following:

1. A correctly named and typed part.
2. A relationship from the correct owner.
3. A content-type registration.
4. Valid XML in the part.
5. Save, reopen, and preservation behavior.

The low-level `examples/ExampleWord/main.cpp` demonstrates creating a package,
styles part, typed WordprocessingML body, table, section properties, save, and
reopen without using the high-level editor.

## Tools, XML, and security

The public `ExyokiOffice::Tools` module provides reusable behavior behind
`exyoki`, including package inspection, validation, archive operations, Flat
OPC conversion, semantic document conversion, document statistics, diffing,
media export, text extraction, replacements, splitting, merging, and resource
deduplication.

`ExyokiOffice::Xml` provides namespace-precise XPath 1.0 queries over package
parts. Prefer it for dynamic queries that do not justify adding a typed
high-level feature.

The three MCP servers under `tools/mcp/` (`exyoki-mcp-word`,
`exyoki-mcp-excel`, `exyoki-mcp-power-point`) expose the same behavior to AI
agents as typed JSON-RPC tools over stdio. They add no library capability: they
are adapters over the editors and `ExyokiOffice::Tools`, with a workspace
sandbox, document sessions with undo, a transactional `batch`, and one result
envelope. New agent-facing behavior belongs in the library or in
`ExyokiOffice::Tools`, not in a server. See `docs/tools/mcp-servers.md`.

`ExyokiOffice::Security` covers signature inspection and verification plus
policy-controlled linked resources. Cryptographic verification depends on an
installed provider. External resolvers may be invoked concurrently and should
be thread-safe. See `docs/Signatures.md` and `docs/ExternalResources.md` before
changing security behavior.

## Repository navigation

| Path | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `include/ExyokiOffice/Word/` | Public high-level Word API |
| `include/ExyokiOffice/Excel/` | Public high-level Excel API |
| `include/ExyokiOffice/PowerPoint/` | Public high-level PowerPoint API |
| `include/ExyokiOffice/Packaging/` | Document parts and lifecycle |
| `include/ExyokiOffice/Tools/` | Reusable package tools |
| `include/ExyokiOffice/Xml/` | Dynamic XPath/query API |
| `include/ExyokiOffice/Security/` | Signatures and external resources |
| `include/ExyokiOffice/DOM/` | Large generated public DOM headers |
| `sources/` | Hand-written implementations plus vendored pugixml and ZIP code |
| `sources/DOM/` | Large generated DOM implementations |
| `gen/` | Native OpenXML source generator |
| `data/` | Imported Open-XML-SDK metadata and local overlays |
| `tools/exyoki/` | Command-line adapter |
| `tools/mcp/` | MCP servers for AI agents and their shared static core |
| `examples/` | Runnable, round-tripping examples |
| `tests/unit/` | doctest tests and regressions |
| `tests/mcp/` | MCP protocol, schema, and per-family tool tests |
| `tests/fuzz/` | fuzz harnesses, curated seeds, and committed crashes |
| `docs/` | User manual and project policies |

## Generated-code rules

Do not edit a file carrying an `<auto-generated>` banner. The main generated
trees are `include/ExyokiOffice/DOM` and `sources/DOM`; several packaging
files are generated as well. Fix generator behavior under `gen/` and regenerate
through the normal CMake build.

Most JSON under `data/` is an imported metadata snapshot. Two overlays are
owned by this repository and must survive imports:

- `data/exyokioffice_part_paths.json` defines absolute per-family folders for
  parts such as media, themes, and charts.
- `data/exyokioffice_ambiguous_elements.json` selects the factory class for
  element names declared by multiple generated classes.

The generator writes to tracked source directories. Inspect `git diff` after a
build. Output must be deterministic across MSVC, GCC, and Clang; explicitly
sort any data whose order affects generated output.

Generated public types must be reachable from a consumer of the shared
library: element and part classes are `EXYOKIOFFICE_EXPORT`, and an enum
class exports `GetMetaEnum()` only, because exporting the class over the
non-exported `OpenXmlEnum` base raises C4275 in the warnings-as-errors
build. An unexported out-of-line member compiles and fails only at link
time outside `sources/`.

For ordinary exploration, exclude generated, metadata, and build trees:

```powershell
rg --files -g '!include/ExyokiOffice/DOM/**' -g '!sources/DOM/**' `
    -g '!data/**' -g '!build/**' -g '!gen/build/**'
```

For one generated symbol, use a targeted search:

```powershell
rg -n "class Paragraph" include/ExyokiOffice/DOM/DocumentFormat/OpenXml/Wordprocessing.hpp
rg -l "SomeOpenXmlType" include/ExyokiOffice/DOM sources/DOM
```

## Build, test, and install

Use checked-in CMake presets. On Windows, `WinBuild.ps1` discovers Visual Studio
with `vswhere`, initializes the developer environment, configures, builds, and
optionally tests or installs:

```powershell
.\WinBuild.ps1 -Configuration Debug -Test
.\WinBuild.ps1 -Clean -Configuration RelWithDebInfo -Test
.\WinBuild.ps1 -Sanitizer Address -Configuration Debug -Test
.\WinBuild.ps1 -Configuration RelWithDebInfo -Install
.\WinBuild.ps1 -Configuration RelWithDebInfo -Install -InstallPrefix C:\ExyokiOffice
```

The default install prefix used with `-Install` is `build/install`. Installation
contains the shared library, public and generated headers, exported CMake
package, `exyoki`, license and project files, and the Markdown documentation.

On Linux:

```bash
cmake --preset linux-ninja-debug
cmake --build --preset linux-ninja-debug
ctest --preset linux-ninja-debug
```

Consumers use the installed target:

```cmake
find_package(ExyokiOffice 1.1 CONFIG REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(MyApplication PRIVATE ExyokiOffice::ExyokiOffice)
```

Set `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` when the installation prefix is outside CMake's normal
search locations.

The library is also a vcpkg port. `vcpkg install exyokioffice` installs the
library alone; `exyoki` and the MCP servers are the optional features `tools`
and `mcp`. Consumers use the same `find_package` call. The port sources live in
a vcpkg registry clone rather than in this repository; `vcpkg/README.md`
describes the layout and `vcpkg/Test-Port.ps1` verifies the package end to end.

The generated translation units make clean builds slow and memory-heavy. Limit
parallel jobs when necessary. On restricted Windows agents, Visual Studio
compiler detection may fail with `MSB4018`, `FileTracker`, and `E_ACCESSDENIED`;
rerun the same preset-based build with sandbox escalation instead of switching
generators.

## Verification expectations

Behavioral changes require focused doctest coverage under `tests/unit`. For
document behavior, test create/open, mutation, save, reopen, and assertions on
the reopened package. This detects missing relationships, content types, and
serialization persistence.

Windows lint commands:

```powershell
.\WinLint.ps1 -Changed -Check
.\WinLint.ps1 -Check
```

Fuzz commands:

```powershell
.\WinFuzz.ps1 -Target flatopc -Seconds 300
.\WinFuzz.ps1 -Replay
.\WinFuzz.ps1 -Target formula -Minimize
```

The growing working corpus stays under `build/<preset>/fuzz-corpus` and is safe
to delete. Curated seeds are under `tests/fuzz/corpus`; `-Minimize` deliberately
updates them. Crash artifacts are stored under `tests/fuzz/crashes` and are
replayed by ordinary unit tests, so committed crashes must not be deleted after
a fix.

## Documentation map

- `README.md`: concise product, quickstart, build, and installation overview.
- `docs/README.md`: complete manual index and required reading order.
- `docs/introduction.md`: scope, architecture, conventions, and package model.
- `docs/Word.md`, `docs/Excel.md`, `docs/PowerPoint.md`: format quickstarts.
- `docs/word/`, `docs/excel/`, `docs/powerpoint/`: task-specific chapters.
- `docs/Compatibility.md`: authoritative feature support and limitations.
- `docs/tools/exyoki.md`: complete CLI reference.
- `docs/tools/conversion-formats.md`: semantic conversion contracts.
- `docs/tools/mcp-servers.md`: the MCP servers, their security model, and the tool catalog of each family.
- `docs/schemas/`: machine-readable contracts, generated by the tool
  (`exyoki schema`) and checked against the library by the test suite.
- `docs/ExternalResources.md`, `docs/Signatures.md`: security-sensitive APIs.
- `docs/Threading.md`: thread-safety, ownership, locking, and cancellation.
- `docs/ABI.md`: versioning and binary compatibility.
- `docs/ci.md`, `docs/fuzzing.md`: verification infrastructure.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: contributor workflow and pull-request checklist.
- `AGENTS.md`: operational source guide for coding agents.

When adding a documentation chapter, update both `docs/README.md` and
`docs/_pdf/chapters.txt`. When feature coverage changes, update
`docs/Compatibility.md` in the same change.

## Contribution constraints

- Public declarations go in `include/ExyokiOffice`; implementations go in
  `sources`.
- Keep `tools/exyoki` thin; reusable logic belongs in the public Tools module.
- Do not modify vendored code unless the task explicitly targets it.
- Preserve C++20, `.clang-format`, strict warnings, and braces on every
  control-flow body.
- Prefer a private helper class with static methods for file-local helpers; do
  not add an anonymous namespace solely for free helper functions.
- Do not commit build products, generated example documents, working fuzz
  corpora, or IDE-local files.
- Update tests, user documentation, compatibility claims, and AI navigation
  files when public behavior or project structure changes.
